system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

We address the issues in the record with respect to the incremental benefits and costs as they pertain to fillable templates below. 41. Benefits of Implementing Fillable Templates. We have already discussed the support for fillable templates in the record and the significant benefits to the public that will accrue, including increased flexibility for alert originators that would result from more effective alerts to the public. We agree that fillable templates, which include ``source, location, and time,'' are ``critical elements'' for optimal WEA messages. Event-specific information also ``contribute[s] to personalization and, thereby, to the effectiveness of the warnings.'' LAAWW supports the Bureau's proposal of the four fillable elements, as ``[e]vent-specific information is extremely beneficial to the public.'' We agree with commenters that the fillable fields allow alert originators to provide more complete, detailed information when they alert the public, and that this information would better equip the public to understand and respond to the alert. We reiterate our belief that form-fillable templates that incorporate the name of the sender, the location, and the time of the disaster (coupled with a description of the threat and the protective action the public should take) create more effective alerts and is consistent with social science research on effective alerting.

data.summary: The alert matches the NCM bulletin. It names the same hazard: fog with visibility that may drop to zero at times. It gives the same window, from 21:30 Tue 17 Feb until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb, and the same area, western regions of the UAE. Certainty 'Likely' and severity 'Moderate' fit a bulletin that says visibility is 'expected to deteriorate' from 'potential fog formation'. The alert uses no unverified inputs.

no_basis.concern: The bulletin says 'several western regions'. The alert says 'western regions of the UAE', which could be read as all western regions. It is a minor broadening, and no specific places are named in either.
no_basis.searched_for: alert area description times consistent with source

no_basis.concern: I could not confirm that severity 'Moderate' matches NCM's own warning level (e.g., a yellow/orange/red scale), because no clause on NCM fog warning levels was returned.
